overall_summary: Bitcoin is reclaiming eighty thousand on a short squeeze and fresh ETF inflows, while a Democratic midterm sweep, softer yields, and weaker oil are fueling a broader risk-on tone. Peace-talk headlines add support, though a lingering exchange hack and NATO strike chatter keep some caution in the mix. Overall the tape leans constructive for crypto into the weekend.
key_points: Spot Bitcoin ETFs flip to net inflows
Midterm blue wave; yields and oil drop
DXY soft; peace talks set for Abu Dhabi
Mercado Bitcoin hack remains an overhang

items.title: Bitcoin Reclaims $80K on Short Squeeze After Midterms
items.summary: Bitcoin bounced hard above eighty thousand dollars after dipping near seventy-five six hundred during the U.S. midterm results. Nearly three hundred seventy-eight million in shorts got liquidated in a single hour, with total crypto liquidations around seven hundred forty million, mostly shorts. Broader markets rallied, oil dropped sharply, and the dollar eased after Democrats swept Congress. Traders should watch resistance at eighty-one to eighty-two thousand; a hold here could flip the recent downtrend, but analysts still flag possible further consolidation.
items.impact: Forced buying and risk-on mood support near-term upside

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Flip to $74.6M Inflows After Heavy Outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded seventy-four point six million in net inflows on November fourth, ending three straight days of withdrawals that totaled about one point one six billion. Fidelity's FBTC led with two hundred thirty-six point seven million in, while BlackRock's IBIT saw two hundred one million out. Ether ETFs also drew positive flows. This mixed but net-positive print signals some institutional demand returning just as price rebounded, so watch if the streak continues into the jobs report.
items.impact: Renewed institutional buying could stabilize or lift BTC

items.title: Trump Media Moves 4,259 BTC Worth $342M to Crypto.com
items.summary: Wallets linked to Trump Media transferred about four thousand two hundred fifty-nine bitcoin, roughly three hundred forty-two to three hundred forty-four million dollars, to a Crypto.com address from convertible-note collateral wallets. The move comes weeks before a possible one-billion-dollar repayment window on November thirtieth. The coins later went to cold storage and the company has previously called similar transfers custody management, not sales. Still, any large transfer to an exchange raises the risk of eventual selling pressure on Bitcoin.
items.impact: Potential supply overhang if sold, but unconfirmed

items.title: Eric Trump's American Bitcoin Posts $126M Q3 Profit
items.summary: American Bitcoin, the miner co-founded by Eric Trump, swung to one hundred twenty-six million dollars in third-quarter net income, driven by a one hundred ninety-seven million dollar gain on its bitcoin holdings. Mining revenue slipped and costs rose, but the company added about four hundred twenty-five bitcoin to end the quarter with eight thousand four hundred twenty-seven BTC. This reinforces the corporate treasury and HODL narrative among public miners even as some pivot to AI.
items.impact: Supports miner accumulation and institutional confidence story

items.title: Hong Kong Passes Crypto Exchange Tax Reporting Law
items.summary: Hong Kong's legislature passed a bill requiring crypto exchanges and service providers to collect customer identity and transaction data starting in twenty twenty-seven under the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework. Automatic sharing with overseas tax authorities begins in twenty twenty-eight. This covers buys, sells, swaps, and external wallet transfers. It brings the hub in line with global tax transparency standards and raises compliance costs, but is not an outright ban or crackdown.
items.impact: Higher compliance burden, limited near-term price effect

items.title: Mercado Bitcoin Hack Continues After Containment Claim
items.summary: A report finds the attack on Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin kept draining funds for hours after the exchange said it was contained, with total losses estimated around forty to forty-eight million dollars across multiple chains. The hacker has been swapping stolen alts for ether. The exchange is starting a phased reopening, pledges to cover customer losses with its own funds, and some stablecoins have been frozen. It is another reminder of exchange security risks so soon after the massive Binance incident.
items.impact: Undermines exchange confidence and highlights ongoing risks

items.title: Democrats Sweep Midterms; Oil Crashes, Yields Drop
items.summary: Democrats took control of both the House and Senate in the US midterms, ending one-party Republican rule. Markets treated it as a de-escalation signal on the Iran conflict, sending Brent crude down nearly nine percent below one hundred dollars, the ten-year yield to around four point eight eight percent, and the dollar index weaker near one oh one point four. Stocks ripped higher with the Dow up three percent. Traders should care because lower oil and yields ease inflation pressure and Fed hike odds, which is classic risk-on fuel for Bitcoin and equities.
items.impact: Supports risk assets via weaker USD, lower yields, and cooler inflation path

items.title: Bank of England Hikes Rates 25bp to 4%
items.summary: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate by a quarter point to four percent in an eight-to-one vote, its first hike in three years. Policymakers cited energy-driven inflation from the Middle East conflict, now expected to push UK CPI toward five percent next year, though second-round effects remain limited so far. The decision was widely priced in. Crypto traders watch it as another major central bank tightening while oil prices tumble, which could limit how far global rates go and keep the focus on US data.
items.impact: GBP supportive locally; limited spillover if oil keeps falling

items.title: US Jobless Claims Edge to 196K; NFP Looms Friday
items.summary: Initial jobless claims for the week ending October thirty-first came in at one hundred ninety-six thousand, almost exactly in line with the one hundred ninety-seven thousand forecast and up slightly from one hundred ninety-four thousand. Continuing claims data was incomplete in early reports. This keeps the labor market looking resilient but not overheating ahead of Friday's full October employment report. Traders care because a soft or hot NFP will swing December Fed hike odds and move the dollar and yields hard.
items.impact: Sets stage for NFP volatility; little immediate directional force

items.title: Q3 Productivity Rises 3.0%; Unit Labor Costs Contained
items.summary: Preliminary nonfarm productivity grew at a three percent annualized rate in the third quarter, well above the prior one point four percent and near the three point one percent consensus. Unit labor costs rose just one point two percent, matching the prior reading and below the one point four percent forecast. Stronger productivity helps contain wage-driven inflation. This is quietly supportive for the soft-landing case and gives the Fed more room if oil-driven price pressures ease.
items.impact: Eases inflation concerns; mildly positive for risk assets and lower-rate bets

items.title: ADP Private Payrolls Beat with 86K Gain
items.summary: ADP reported private employers added eighty-six thousand jobs in October, beating the roughly sixty-seven to seventy-five thousand forecasts and matching the revised prior month. Services did most of the heavy lifting while goods-producing hiring stayed soft. It is an imperfect NFP predictor but keeps the labor market from looking weak heading into Friday's official report. A firm print tomorrow would keep December Fed hike odds elevated even after the oil drop.
items.impact: Supports resilient labor narrative; focus remains on Friday NFP

items.title: Ten-Year Yield Near 4.88%, DXY Soft Around 101.4
items.summary: The US ten-year Treasury yield settled near four point eight eight percent after sliding on the midterm results and oil plunge, while the dollar index hovered around one hundred one point four to one hundred one point five. Markets still price a decent chance of a December Fed hike but the drop in energy prices is chipping away at those odds. For crypto traders this combination of softer dollar and lower real yields has historically been a tailwind once the dust settles.
items.impact: Weaker USD and lower yields constructive for Bitcoin and risk assets

items.title: Democrats Sweep US Midterms in Blue Wave
items.summary: Democrats have seized control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm victory that serves as a clear rebuke to President Trump. Trump himself acknowledged the Iran war and the resulting surge in gas prices played a major role in the Republican losses. For traders this matters because it raises the odds of political gridlock, reduced appetite for further military escalation, and potential pressure to wind down the Middle East conflict that has crushed energy markets and risk assets.
items.impact: Risk-on rally as oil falls and escalation fears ease

items.title: Oil Plunges 20% This Week on Iran De-escalation Bets
items.summary: Brent crude has crashed nearly 20 percent this week, falling below 100 dollars a barrel for the first time in months, as markets bet the midterm defeat will force Trump toward a negotiated exit from the Iran war rather than fresh strikes. The Strait of Hormuz remains heavily disrupted with fresh reports of tankers catching fire after hitting mines or projectiles. Crypto and risk assets should watch closely because sustained lower oil eases inflation pressure and supports broader risk appetite, though any sudden re-escalation could reverse it fast.
items.impact: Lower energy prices support stocks, bonds and Bitcoin

items.title: US-Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks Set for Abu Dhabi
items.summary: The United States, Russia and Ukraine will hold working-level trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 aimed at security guarantees, de-escalation and ending the war. Kremlin confirmed the meeting with Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky leading the Russian side, while Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner represent Washington; parallel Brussels talks cover reconstruction. Traders should care because any credible progress reduces European energy and geopolitical risk premiums that have weighed on global markets for years.
items.impact: Potential de-risking of Europe and energy markets

items.title: Ukrainian Drones Ignite Major Russian Oil Refinery
items.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the large Rosneft Ryazan oil refinery overnight, sparking a major fire at a plant that processes over 17 million tons of crude a year and supplies the Moscow region. It is the latest in a wave of attacks that have hit multiple Russian refineries in recent days, compounding earlier damage. This keeps pressure on Russian refined product exports and global diesel markets even as crude prices fall on Iran hopes, creating mixed signals for energy traders and inflation expectations.
items.impact: Tightens refined products supply amid crude weakness

items.title: NATO Drafts Plans for Deep Strikes Inside Russia
items.summary: According to fresh reporting, NATO is developing defense plans that would respond to a Russian attack on alliance territory with conventional precision strikes deep inside Russia against bases, supply depots and industrial facilities. Supreme Allied Commander Europe outlined a theory of victory focused on breaking the enemy warfighting system far behind the front lines. This raises the long-term escalation ceiling in Europe and could keep defense and geopolitical risk premiums elevated even if Ukraine talks advance.
items.impact: Elevates long-term Europe escalation risk premium

items.title: Trump Says US Ends $4 Billion Annual Aid to Israel
items.summary: President Trump announced a deal with Prime Minister Netanyahu to stop roughly 4 billion dollars in annual US military aid to Israel by the end of 2026, saying Israel no longer needs it and can still buy American weapons. The existing memorandum runs to 2028 so implementation details remain unclear and Congress may push back. For markets this signals a potential shift in US Middle East posture after the midterms and could add another layer of uncertainty to an already volatile region.
items.impact: Adds uncertainty to US-Israel alliance and regional dynamics
